cf.title: Add PQTRACE env to enable protocol tracing in libpq

input.subject: Add PQTRACE env to enable protocol tracing in libpq

verdict_reasoning: The goal is stated and has support: message #2 gives a +1 and P1 shows an earlier attempt at the same need. No surviving objection questions the idea. Four fixable design points remain at level 2. The decisive one is security-1: trace_file opens a file, and dblink and postgres_fdw pass user-supplied options to libpq inside the server. standards-compat-2 and standards-compat-3 concern names and the stdout target, which are hard to change after release.

brief.title: Enable libpq protocol tracing via environment variable or connection parameter
brief.problem: Protocol tracing in libpq starts only when the application calls PQtrace(), so psql and other existing clients cannot use it without code changes. The libpq_pipeline test also misses startup packets because it calls PQtrace() after the connection exists. The target users are developers who debug protocol behavior and write tests.
brief.proposed_design: libpq gains the connection parameters trace_file and trace_flags and the environment variables PQTRACE and PQTRACEFLAGS, and calls PQtrace() while it processes connection options, before the first packet. Supporting patches make fe-trace.c write each line with one fwrite, add regress masks for StartupMessage and ParameterStatus, and print the cancel key as hex. libpq_pipeline switches to trace_file.
user_visible_surface: Connection parameter trace_file: a file path, or "-" for stdout.
Connection parameter trace_flags: integer bitmask, 1 for PQTRACE_SUPPRESS_TIMESTAMPS, 2 for PQTRACE_REGRESS_MODE.
Environment variables PQTRACE and PQTRACEFLAGS, equal to trace_file and trace_flags.
Trace output change: the cancel key in BackendKeyData and CancelRequest prints as hex only.
Regress mode now masks parameter values and packet length in StartupMessage and ParameterStatus.
author_claims: Tracing becomes usable from psql and any libpq application without code changes.
libpq_pipeline gets simpler and gains test coverage of startup packets.
Writing each trace line with one fwrite stops interleaving when several connections trace to stdout.
The limits are acceptable for a debugging tool: no shared trace file, and no tracing of cancel connections when the target is a file.
The feature allows a future regress-style harness that compares SQL scripts against expected traces.
brief.thread_state: Jelte Fennema-Nio gave a strong +1 for the idea but has not reviewed the patches. No technical review is visible, and the entry has moved to a second CommitFest.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether trace_file in a connection string from an untrusted source can make a client create or overwrite any writable file.
The commit message, the docs and the thread disagree on whether the feature is environment variables only or connection parameters too.
The proposal does not say why the variables use the PQ prefix when other libpq environment variables use PG.
The proposal does not say whether libpq truncates or appends to the trace file, or when it closes the file.
The proposal does not say how tracing behaves across multiple hosts, reconnects or connection retries.
The proposal does not say whether the trace format, now used in expected test output, becomes a stable interface.

prior_attempts.title: libpq trace log
prior_attempts.quote: This seems to make pg_conn much larger than we'd like.
prior_attempts.reason: Earlier, David Steele moved the patch to PG13 because, in agreement with Andres, it was not clear where the patch was going. The last message before the decision is a review by Alvaro Herrera, who agreed with the one-line-per-message direction but asked for changes. He objected to a frontend_entry[MAXPGPATH] array in pg_conn and listed smaller fixes. The thread shows no new patch or author reply after that review before the entry was returned.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 started as a query log enabled by connection parameters or environment variables, then narrowed to reworking PQtrace() output and deferred the no-recompile part. This proposal does that deferred part on top of the one-line-per-message format.

objections.title: trace_file lets dblink and postgres_fdw users write server files
objections.failure_scenario: A non-superuser with EXECUTE on dblink_connect, or a postgres_fdw user mapping, passes trace_file=$PGDATA/postgresql.auto.conf. The backend opens that path as the postgres OS user, truncating or overwriting it. The admin finds out at the next restart or reload.
objections.argument: dblink and postgres_fdw run libpq inside the server and pass user-supplied connection options to it, so a libpq option that opens a file becomes a server-side file write. Today these modules hide only debug options and a short exclusion list. The patch prose does not say whether trace_file is marked as a debug option, nor does it mention dblink, postgres_fdw or other in-server libpq callers. The same issue applies to applications that accept connection URIs from end users.
objections.author_must_show: How is trace_file kept out of connection strings that dblink, postgres_fdw and other in-server or multi-tenant libpq callers accept from less privileged users?

critic.reasoning: dblink and postgres_fdw accept libpq options from users and filter only debug options and a short list. The patch prose does not say that trace_file is a debug option or that in-server callers reject it.

objections.title: Trace to stdout by default mixes protocol lines into program output
objections.failure_scenario: A developer exports PQTRACE=- in a shell to debug psql and later runs pg_dump > db.sql or psql -At -c ... | script in the same shell. Trace lines go into the dump or the piped data, and the user finds out when restore or the script fails.
objections.argument: An environment variable is inherited by every libpq program started afterwards, and many of them write their real output to stdout. Postgres client tools send diagnostics to stderr. The only special value the proposal offers is "-" for stdout, and message #1 shows it as the main usage.
objections.author_must_show: Why should the special value send traces to stdout and not to stderr, given pg_dump and psql scripts write data to stdout?

critic.reasoning: The user sets the variable, but child programs such as pg_dump inherit it and write their data to stdout. The proposal offers no stderr target and does not say why stdout is the special value.

objections.title: PQTRACE breaks the PG prefix and parameter-name pairing of libpq environment variables
objections.failure_scenario: A user who knows PGSSLMODE and PGAPPNAME sets PGTRACE or PGTRACEFILE, and nothing happens. Tools that clear or list libpq settings by matching PG* environment variables miss PQTRACE, so tracing leaks into their child processes.
objections.argument: Every libpq environment variable in the docs section the patch edits uses the PG prefix and mostly mirrors its parameter name, for example sslmode and PGSSLMODE. The patch pairs trace_file with PQTRACE and trace_flags with PQTRACEFLAGS. Message #1 and the commit message call the feature env vars only, while the doc hunk also adds connection parameters, so the thread has not settled the names. Once released, they cannot be renamed without breaking scripts.
objections.author_must_show: Why not use PGTRACEFILE and PGTRACEFLAGS, matching the parameter names and the existing PG prefix?

critic.reasoning: The doc hunk adds PQTRACE to a list where every other variable uses the PG prefix, and message #1 gives no reason. The thread has no reply on naming, so the consistency question stands.

objections.title: Startup packets in expected traces couple tests to build and server settings
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch marks a new GUC as GUC_REPORT, or changes SSL or GSS negotiation, and nine libpq_pipeline trace files fail. A buildfarm animal built with GSSAPI, or without SSL, sends a different startup sequence and goes red although nothing is broken.
objections.argument: Patch 0006 adds startup messages to nine expected trace files. Patch 0002 masks parameter values and packet length, but the sequence of messages stays in the expected output. That sequence depends on build options, sslmode, gssencmode, the protocol version and the set of reported GUCs. Every later patch that adds a reported parameter or a negotiation step must update these files, and the proposal does not say how build-dependent messages are kept out of the expected output.
objections.author_must_show: How do the expected traces stay stable across SSL and GSSAPI builds, and what must a patch that adds a GUC_REPORT setting update?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 shows SSLRequest in the trace, and that line depends on the build and on TCP or Unix socket use. Patch 0002 masks values and lengths only, so the message sequence stays in nine expected files.

refuted.title: trace_file in server-side connection strings lets users write server files
refuted.failure_scenario: A non-superuser who may use dblink, or who holds pg_create_subscription, puts trace_file=/path/inside/PGDATA in a connection string. The backend opens that path as the server OS user and writes protocol traces into it. A subscription keeps the string, so pg_dump carries it to the restored cluster.
refuted.argument: The patch makes trace_file an ordinary connection parameter, and the docs list it next to load_balance_hosts. Server code passes user-supplied connection strings to libpq: dblink, postgres_fdw, subscriptions and primary_conninfo. Message #1 and the commit message discuss psql and test harnesses only, and say nothing about libpq running inside the server or about which callers must reject the new keyword. A committer would likely ask for this before the parameter exists at all.
refuted.author_must_show: Which server-side libpq callers will reject trace_file and trace_flags, and how does a non-superuser connection string get prevented from naming a server file?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of security-1, which states the same server-side file write with a sharper scenario. The subscription and pg_dump points fall under its question about other in-server libpq callers.

refuted.title: Server-side libpq users such as walreceiver would also start tracing
refuted.failure_scenario: A developer exports PQTRACE in the shell that starts a standby, or a subscription owner puts trace_file in the CONNECTION string. The walreceiver or the apply worker then writes every replication message to that file or to postmaster stdout, with no rotation. The disk fills, or several workers overwrite one file, and the operator finds out only when the standby stops.
refuted.argument: The patch hooks tracing into connection option processing in fe-connect.c, so every libpq consumer inside the server inherits it. That includes primary_conninfo, create subscription, postgres_fdw and dblink. Message #1 says that several connections sharing one file is unsupported, and server processes are the common case for that. The proposal does not say whether trace_file is a debug option that these callers reject, or whether they ignore PQTRACE.
refuted.author_must_show: How do walreceiver, logical replication workers, postgres_fdw and dblink handle trace_file and PQTRACE, and does any of them reject it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of security-1 for the subscription owner case. The rest is an operator who sets a debug variable for the server and gets the trace that was asked for, which is not a failure.

refuted.title: Inherited PQTRACE writes passwords and row data to files
refuted.failure_scenario: A developer exports PQTRACE in a shell profile or CI job. Every child libpq program, including pg_dump and cron scripts, then writes PasswordMessage contents, query texts and DataRow values to that file. The file is created with the process umask, possibly readable by other local users, and the leak is noticed only later.
refuted.argument: Today an application calls PQtrace() itself and chooses the stream, so it decides the exposure. An environment variable turns tracing on implicitly for every process that inherits it. Regress mode masks StartupMessage and ParameterStatus but does not mask authentication messages or result data. The proposal also does not say whether libpq creates the file with restrictive permissions or whether it truncates or appends.
refuted.author_must_show: Which file mode does libpq use when it creates the trace file, and are authentication messages masked or omitted when tracing is enabled from the environment?

critic.reasoning: The user who sets PQTRACE owns the traced processes and asks for the trace, and umask applies as it does to pg_dump -f output. The trace content is what PQtrace() already prints today.

refuted.title: PQTRACE names break the PG prefix convention and become permanent
refuted.failure_scenario: Users and scripts start to depend on PQTRACE and PQTRACEFLAGS in release 20. If the project later wants names that match PGSSLMODE, PGAPPNAME and the other libpq variables, it must keep both forms or break those scripts.
refuted.argument: Every other libpq environment variable uses the PG prefix, and patch 0005 documents PQTRACE next to them in the same list. Message #1 does not say why the PQ prefix was chosen. Once released, these names cannot be removed without a deprecation cycle. The commit message speaks of environment variables only, while the docs add trace_file and trace_flags, so the proposal does not yet say which surface is the primary one.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should these variables use PQ instead of PG, given that every other libpq environment variable uses PG?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which makes the same PG prefix point with a more concrete question.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: walreceiver and logical replication workers connect through libpq, so they also process trace_file and PQTRACE.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: see objection maintenance-fit-1: Startup packets in expected traces couple tests to build and server settings

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: PQTRACE="-" writes trace lines to stdout of psql and of every other libpq client that inherits the variable.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: trace_file makes libpq open a file named in a connection string, including strings that dblink and postgres_fdw accept from users.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Two connection parameters and two environment variables become permanent, and nine expected trace files now include startup messages.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: How is trace_file kept out of connection strings that dblink, postgres_fdw and other in-server libpq callers accept from less privileged users?
Why does the special value "-" send the trace to stdout and not to stderr, given that pg_dump and psql scripts write data to stdout?
Why are the variables named PQTRACE and PQTRACEFLAGS, and not PGTRACEFILE and PGTRACEFLAGS to match the parameter names and the PG prefix?
How do the expected traces in libpq_pipeline stay the same across builds with and without SSL or GSSAPI, and when a new GUC_REPORT setting is added?
Does libpq truncate or append to the trace file, when does it close the file, and what happens on a retry with multiple hosts?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows libpq connection option handling and the in-server libpq callers (dblink, postgres_fdw, walreceiver) would have to own it. Nobody has reviewed the patches in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a connection parameter that opens files, for as long as libpq keeps it. The owner also signs for the names of two environment variables and for trace output that expected test files now depend on.
committability.author_follow_up: The author moved the entry to the next CommitFest on 2026-10-02. The thread has no author reply after message #1.

priority.reason: The feature serves developers who debug the protocol or write tests, and it has a +1 in message #2. The series is six patches limited to libpq and one test module, but the file-write question in security-1 and the names should be settled before code review.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so it is unknown whether trace_file is marked as a debug option, which dblink and postgres_fdw already hide. The file open mode and the handling of connection retries could not be checked either.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: libpq trace log
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch began as a libpq client-side query log enabled by connection parameters or environment variables (logdir/PGLOGDIR, logsize/PGLOGSIZE). After review it was narrowed to reworking PQtrace() so it prints one line per protocol message with a timestamp, and enabling it without recompiling was deferred.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Earlier, David Steele moved the patch to PG13 because, in agreement with Andres, it was not clear where the patch was going. The last message before the decision is a review by Alvaro Herrera, who agreed with the one-line-per-message direction but asked for changes. He objected to a frontend_entry[MAXPGPATH] array in pg_conn and listed smaller fixes. The thread shows no new patch or author reply after that review before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This seems to make pg_conn much larger than we'd like.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_tracing
precedents_retrieved.summary: A contrib-style extension, pg_tracing, generates distributed-tracing spans for planner, executor and nested queries, using trace context passed in SQLCommenter comments or a sampling rate. Spans go into a shared memory buffer, and an external forwarder reads them with pg_tracing_consume_spans() and sends them to a trace collector.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas recommended that the author publish pg_tracing as a separate extension on GitHub, and Nikita Malakhov agreed. Heikki's own message is not shown; only the replies quote it. In March 2024 the author said he was moving pg_tracing to a GitHub repository, and the entry was later withdrawn. The visible messages do not show a technical objection that blocked the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: To give a quick update: following Heikki's suggestion, I'm currently working on getting pg_tracing as a separate extension on github.

precedents_retrieved.title: meson/testwrap: support EXTRA_REGRESS_OPTS environment variable
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes meson's testwrap read EXTRA_REGRESS_OPTS and append its contents to the regress, isolation and ecpg test commands, as autoconf does. This lets a user run the full schedule with extra pg_regress options, such as --use-existing against a running instance.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it because Andreas Karlsson already had a patch for the same feature in the current commitfest. That patch was described as reviewed well and only missing documentation. No one objected to the design.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I already have a patch[1] for this in the current commitfest which
people think looks good other than that it lacks documentation, which I
think is a fair complaint.

precedents_retrieved.title: Report tranche ID and LWLock pointer in LWLock static tracepoints
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds the LWLock pointer and the numeric tranche ID to each LWLock static tracepoint, so traces can tell individual locks apart and compare them across processes. It also fixes misplaced tracepoints, adds a single tracepoint for all acquires and releases plus start markers for timing, and adds comments on LWLock tranches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Two parts were committed by Peter Eisentraut: the removal of the wrong lwlock__acquire tracepoint in LWLockWaitForVar, and the move of TRACE_POSTGRESQL_LWLOCK_RELEASE. In his last review he reported that patch 0002 did not build on macOS because uint64 was used in the probe definitions, and that the probe changes had no documentation. He also asked for a different argument order and whether both tranche name and tranche ID are needed. The visible messages show no new version after that review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
First, a problem:  0002 doesn't build on macOS, because uint64 has been
used in the probe definitions.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make installcheck-world in a clean environment
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets "make installcheck-world" work after "make clean" or against installed binary packages. A USE_INSTALLED_ASSETS flag makes installcheck build and run tests with the installed ecpg, headers, libraries and pg_regress instead of the build tree.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it after several commitfests because no reviewer or committer took it up. Tom Lane and Michael Paquier held that installcheck is meant to test something already built, so its dependence on "make all" is acceptable. Tom Lane also found the patch invasive outside ecpg and undocumented. When closing, he wrote that only the author was unhappy with the current behavior.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think the fundamental problem here is that nobody except Alexander
is unhappy with the current behavior of "make installcheck", and it
is not very clear whether this patch might change the behavior in
ways that do make others unhappy.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "libpqwalreceiver: Convert to libpq-be-fe-helpers.h"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "libpqwalreceiver: Convert to libpq-be-fe-helpers.h"
Reverted commit(s): libpqwalreceiver: Convert to libpq-be-fe-helpers.h
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 728f86fec65537eade8d9e751961782ddb527934.

The signal handling was a few bricks shy of a load in that commit,
which made the walreceiver non-responsive to SIGTERM while it was
waiting for the connection to be established. That prevented a standby
from being promoted.

Since it was non-essential refactoring, let's revert it to make v16
work the same as earlier releases. I reverted it in 'master' too, to
keep the branches in sync. The refactoring was a good idea as such,
but it needs a bit more work. Once we have developed a complete patch
with this issue fixed, let's re-apply that to 'master'.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add max_wal_replay_size connection parameter to libpq
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a libpq connection parameter, max_wal_replay_size, that runs a query during connection setup and skips a standby whose pg_last_wal_receive_lsn() minus pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() exceeds the threshold. A standby with a NULL receive LSN is treated as over the threshold, and the connection fails if no host qualifies.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. SATYANARAYANA NARLAPURAM objected that a standby with no WAL receiver can still be current while replaying archived WAL. He also said measuring only local apply lag does not route clients to the freshest standby. The thread ends with the author's reply on 2026-03-30, and the entry was withdrawn in July with no further message shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert non-text output formats for pg_dumpall
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert non-text output formats for pg_dumpall
Reverted commit(s): Add non-text output formats to pg_dumpall; Clean up nodes that  are no longer of use in 007_pgdumpall.pl; Fix casting away const-ness in pg_restore.c; Improve writing map.dat preamble; pg_restore: add --no-globals option to skip globals
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts the non-text (custom/directory/tar) output format support
for pg_dumpall added by 763aaa06f03 and its feature-specific follow-ups,
in line with Noah Misch's post-commit review which recommends reverting
and finishing the work through the commitfest.

Scope is deliberately minimal: only the feature itself is removed.
Independent improvements that merely touched the same files, or that were
committed alongside the feature but do not depend on its design, are
preserved.

Reverted (the feature):

  763aaa06f03  Add non-text output formats to pg_dumpall
  d6d9b96b404  Clean up nodes that are no longer of use in 007_pgdumpall.pl
  01c729e0c7a  Fix casting away const-ness in pg_restore.c
  c7572cd48d3  Improve writing map.dat preamble
  3c19983cc08  pg_restore: add --no-globals option to skip globals
  abff4492d02  Fix options listing of pg_restore --no-globals
  bb53b8d359d  Fix small memory leak in get_dbname_oid_list_from_mfile()
  a793677e57b  pg_restore: Remove dead code in restore_all_databases()
  a198c26dede  pg_dumpall: simplify coding of dropDBs()
  ec80215c033  pg_restore: Remove unnecessary strlen() calls in options parsing

Preserved (independent of the feature):

  b2898baaf7e  the check_mut_excl_opts() helper in src/fe_utils/option_utils.c
               and its use in pg_dump
  7c8280eeb58  pg_dump's conflicting-option refactor (and tests 002/005)
  be0d0b457cb  pg_dumpall's rejection of --clean together with --data-only
               (re-expressed directly, since pg_dumpall.c is otherwise
               returned to its pre-feature state)
  74b4438a70b  the dangling-grantor-OID GRANT fix (back-patched through 16)
  273d26b75e7, d4cb9c37765  independent pg_restore.sgml clarifications

Because the feature restructured pg_dumpall.c and pg_restore.c (pg_restore's
main() was split into restore_one_database() plus a dispatcher) and
interleaved its option checks with the conflicting-option refactor in the
same regions, the cosmetic check_mut_excl_opts() reflow of those two files'
option blocks is inseparable from the feature and comes out with it; the
behavior is unchanged.  The reusable helper and pg_dump's use of it are
unaffected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add new protocol message to make GUC_REPORT configurable and use it for psql prompt substitution of %N with the current user
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a psql prompt escape %N that shows the current role. To keep the prompt current, it adds a new protocol message and libpq functions (PQlinkParameterStatus, PQunlinkParameterStatus) that turn GUC_REPORT on or off for a given setting during a session.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch and said he would resend it once Jelte Fennema-Nio's _pq_.report_parameters patch is committed. Peter Eisentraut suggested a GUC that lists the settings to report instead of a new protocol message. Jelte Fennema-Nio argued that proxies such as PgBouncer already re-sync GUCs, so a GUC-based design is less fragile for them than a new message type with its own connection state.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think this is probably one of the core reasons why I would very much prefer GUCs over new message types to configure protocol extensions like this: It means proxies would not to keep track of and re-sync a new kind of connection state every time a protocol extension is added.

precedents_retrieved.title: improve DEBUG1 logging of parallel workers for CREATE INDEX
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the DEBUG1 message for parallel CREATE INDEX to report parallel workers launched as well as planned. It later grew into a CREATE INDEX (VERBOSE) option, with matching REINDEX (VERBOSE) output, that reports parallel worker use at INFO level.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it after Michael Paquier pointed to Tom's view that such details should come from an extended EXPLAIN rather than VERBOSE options on more commands. Michael also asked how clients would consume the output. The author wrote that the best approach needs more discussion, and that fixing only the REINDEX DEBUG1 output did not make much sense.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm +-0 about the
VERBOSE option attached to more commands, as it is a bit harder for
clients to catch the information wanted.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert 019_replslot_limit.pl related debugging aids.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert 019_replslot_limit.pl related debugging aids.
Reverted commit(s): Don't fail for > 1 walsenders in 019_replslot_limit, add debug messages.; Add retries for further investigation of 019_replslot_limit.pl failures.; Add further debug info to help debug 019_replslot_limit.pl failures.; Add temporary debug info to help debug 019_replslot_limit.pl failures.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts most of 91c0570a791, f28bf667f60, fe0972ee5e6, afdeff10526. The
only thing left is the retry loop in 019_replslot_limit.pl that avoids
spurious failures by retrying a couple times.

We haven't seen any hard evidence that this is caused by anything but slow
process shutdown. We did not find any cases where walsenders did not vanish
after waiting for longer. Therefore there's no reason for this debugging code
to remain.

Pipelining/batch mode support for libpq
Threads: PATCH: Batch/pipelining support for libpq

roaster_notes.note: P1's recorded reason concerns a fixed MAXPGPATH array in pg_conn. That is an implementation detail, and nothing in this proposal's prose shows the same choice. Message #1 points to an earlier thread about BackendKeyData tracing as the first posting of this patchset; the thread reports no rejection there.
Three objections raised. The hex cancel key and new regress masks change trace output, but tracing is a debugging aid, so I did not count that as a compatibility break.

The proposal changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog or wire message. The pg_conn change sits in libpq-int.h and is not public ABI. The only point in this angle is server processes that use libpq.
Two security objections are raised. Both depend on code that was not shown, such as the option's dispchar and the file open mode, so they are provisional.
No hot-path objection: the extra work runs only when tracing is enabled. No committer has reviewed the patches yet, which affects committability but not the verdict.

No existing feature does this job. Postgres has no way to start PQtrace() in an unmodified client such as psql. psql -L logs queries and results, not protocol messages. Wireshark with the PostgreSQL dissector needs capture privileges, does not see Unix-socket traffic, and needs TLS keys (sslkeylogfile). Its output also cannot serve as expected test output. For the libpq_pipeline part only, calling PQtrace() between PQconnectStartParams() and PQconnectPoll() could capture startup packets without a new option, but that does not help psql. No extension or hook covers this, so from this angle the gap is real.

Demand looks sufficient for a small developer tool: message #2 adds a second voice, and [P1] shows an earlier attempt to enable libpq tracing without recompiling. The in-tree libpq_pipeline test is a concrete consumer that gains startup-packet coverage. Non-users pay little, mostly two connection parameters and two environment variables, and the one design issue for this angle (the PQ prefix) belongs to other angles.
